decisions.summary: Implementation fix is already landed in commit bd7d00787 — this issue's remaining work is tests + verification only.

Add a new dedicated CLI test file at src/cli/commands/__tests__/kill.test.ts rather than extending an existing one — no kill.test.ts exists today and a focused file keeps the docker-teardown contract auditable.

Extend the existing src/dashboard/server/routes/__tests__/agents-lifecycle-event.test.ts with docker-teardown cases rather than creating a new file — it already mocks getAgentStateAsync/stopAgentAsync/appendAgentLifecycleLog and provides the createAgentStopHandler runner, so reusing it minimizes test infrastructure.

Assert behavior by spying on stopWorkspaceDocker (and findWorkspacePath / resolveProjectFromIssue) call arguments — that is the smallest verifiable contract proving the fix and the only way to assert on the route's dynamic imports.

Cover the central regression in a single test bead per surface with two acceptance subItems (specialist + work) — both cases share identical mock scaffolding; splitting them would create duplicate-setup beads.

Record the manual dashboard-stop verification as a docs/manual-tests/PAN-1326.md recipe (steps + expected docker ps before/after evidence) so the human verifier has a fixed playbook to run post-merge. The work agent cannot drive a live browser autonomously, so the equivalent code-level proof comes from bead 2 (route handler test).

hazards.summary: The dashboard route uses dynamic `await import(...)` for resolveProjectFromIssue and findWorkspacePath inside an inner Effect.promise. Static `vi.mock('../../../lib/projects.js', ...)` and `vi.mock('../../../lib/lifecycle/archive-planning.js', ...)` from the route test file MUST still intercept these dynamic imports (vitest's module registry resolves both static and dynamic specifiers through the same mock graph).
hazards.mitigation: Use the exact specifier strings the route uses (`../../../lib/projects.js` and `../../../lib/lifecycle/archive-planning.js`) when declaring vi.mock from the test file. Confirm with a sanity-check test that the mocked function is called when stateBeforeStop has issueId.

hazards.summary: stopWorkspaceDocker uses existsSync on the real filesystem — if a test mock returns a real path that doesn't exist, the function will silently no-op with containersFound=false but won't throw. That can mask a fix regression if the test only asserts on console.log.
hazards.mitigation: Assert directly on the stopWorkspaceDocker mock's call arguments (workspacePath + issueLower) — NOT on side effects like console output or DockerCleanupResult.containersFound. The contract under test is 'we resolved the right path and called stopWorkspaceDocker with it', not 'docker actually ran'.

hazards.summary: The work-agent regression case must use a state.workspace value that differs from what findWorkspacePath returns — otherwise the test would pass even if the code reverted to reading state.workspace. The regression has to assert on the resolver's output, not on equality between the two.
hazards.mitigation: In the work-agent test, set state.workspace='/orchestrator/path' but mock findWorkspacePath to return '/resolved/by/issue/path'. Assert stopWorkspaceDocker was called with '/resolved/by/issue/path' (the resolver's output), proving state.workspace was NOT used.

hazards.summary: kill.ts uses CommonJS-style imports of resolveProjectFromIssue and findWorkspacePath at the top of the file. The test must vi.mock these modules BEFORE the import of killCommand, otherwise the real implementations bind.
hazards.mitigation: Follow the close.test.ts pattern: vi.hoisted({ ... }) for the mock fns, vi.mock declarations using importActual passthrough where needed, THEN import { killCommand } from '../kill.js' at the bottom of the mock block.

hazards.summary: process.exit(1) is called by kill.ts if stopAgent throws — tests must not let that escape and abort the suite.
hazards.mitigation: Mock stopAgent to resolve successfully in the happy-path tests. If a test needs the error branch, stub process.exit with vi.spyOn(process, 'exit').mockImplementation(() => undefined as never).

hazards.summary: The fix preserves the issueId? null-guard — if state has no issueId, docker teardown is skipped silently. Tests should include a no-issueId case so the guard doesn't get removed accidentally during a future refactor.
hazards.mitigation: Add a third subItem to each bead asserting that when state.issueId is undefined, stopWorkspaceDocker is NOT called at all (the issue gate is upstream of the resolver chain).
